title: compact-block-allocator: adaptive compaction and reuse windows for paged KV
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Adaptive KV block compaction and reuse windowing to reduce fragmentation and improve p99 latencies; new kv.* runtime metrics; safe rollout behind feature flag.
commits: a1c3b5f: introduce CompactBlockAllocator and basic reuse window
b4d2f9e: add compaction worker with throttling and util_percent guard
c7e9a11: batching scheduler hook + pre-pin predictor integration
d2f6e48: metrics and tests; tune default thresholds
review_comments: Matt Cheng: Can we avoid compaction during short GC spikes? Suggest adding an exponential backoff after a compaction run.
Author (Aisha): Added throttling in compaction_worker and a cooldown backoff; defaults conservatively to avoid repeated compactions.
Ravi Singh: Are there any workloads where reuse window increases p99? We should test heavy-shuffle inference.

Author (Aisha): Bench included heavy-shuffle trace (kv_fragmentation_bench) showing reuse window reduces fragmentation and yields 8-12% p99 improvement for long-context chat; we also add a flag to disable reuse window per-deployment.
Lena Ortiz: minor nit: metric name kv.compaction_ops should be a counter; kv.fragmentation_ratio gauge looks good.
Author (Aisha): Fixed metric types and added tags (pool, model_family).
ci_checks: bench: perf benchmark run attached (see artifacts)
benchmarks: baseline: main at 2026-01-20 (no compaction), p99 120ms, token-cost baseline
this-PR: p99 106-110ms on long-context chat traces (8-12% improvement), average token cost down ~17% in fragment-heavy workload
notes: small context (<512) saw negligible diff; heavy-shuffle trace saw fragmentation_ratio fall from 0.38 to 0.12 after 6 hours
rollout_plan: canary: enable for 5% of traffic on Dedicated pools for 24h
auto-rollback: if p99 increases by >5% over baseline or compaction_ops > expected threshold
merge_outcome: squash-merge by Matt Cheng; commit message summarises adaptive compaction + reuse window; changelog entry added to releases/CHANGELOG.md
notes: This PR intentionally keeps compaction conservative; future follow-ups planned: (1) finer-grained kernel-side prefetch when contiguous mapping present, (2) a cooperative compaction shim for multi-tenant pools, (3) eviction-aware pin scoring. See docs/architecture/kv_compaction.md for details.
